records.title: 1.0L EcoBoost Degas Hose Coolant Loss & "EcoBoom" Overheating Engine Failure
records.description: The 1.0L EcoBoost uses a brittle nylon degas/coolant return hose running from the top of the expansion tank to the engine. Over thousands of heat cycles the nylon becomes brittle and cracks or snaps, often at highway speed. Because the engine has a very small coolant capacity and high thermal load, a burst hose causes total coolant loss in seconds; the aluminum cylinder head then overheats almost instantly, warps, and blows the head gasket — the failure mode owners nickname 'EcoBoom.' Ford issued safety action 17S09 (and related regional campaigns) to replace the brittle nylon hose with a reinforced rubberized version, and in the UK agreed to fund repairs after a wave of overheating fires. Owners are advised to check whether the hose from the expansion tank is hard black plastic (original, at-risk) or flexible rubber (updated).
records.solution: Replace the original nylon degas hose with the updated reinforced/rubberized part under the Ford field service action where eligible. Inspect the coolant expansion tank hose material; if hard black plastic, replace proactively. If overheating already occurred, pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the cylinder head for warping — a warped head requires machining or head replacement plus a new head gasket. Always refill and bleed the small-capacity system correctly to avoid air locks.
symptoms: Sudden coolant loss / low coolant warning
Temperature gauge spiking or overheating warning
Steam or coolant smell from engine bay
White smoke from exhaust after overheat
Visible cracked or split hard-plastic coolant hose

records.title: 1.6L EcoBoost Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup (Direct Injection)
records.description: Like other direct-injection engines, the Fiesta ST's 1.6L EcoBoost has no fuel washing over the back of the intake valves, so oil vapor from the PCV system bakes into carbon deposits on the valves and ports over time. Owner tear-down 'case reports' confirm measurable buildup that restricts airflow, typically noticeable by ~60k–80k miles as rough idle, hesitation, and reduced throttle response. It is less severe than some VW/Audi DI engines but is a well-known maintenance item; oils with a low NOACK volatility rating slow the accumulation.
records.solution: Walnut-blast (media-blast) the intake valves and ports to remove carbon — commonly done around 60k–80k miles. Reduce future buildup by fitting an oil catch can, using low-NOACK oil, and keeping up with oil changes. An intake/induction cleaning can help mildly but does not fully remove hardened deposits the way walnut blasting does.

records.title: Blend Door Actuator Failure — Stuck on Heat or Cold
records.description: The Ford Fiesta is prone to blend door actuator failure, which controls the mix of hot and cold air in the HVAC system. When the actuator motor or its plastic gears fail, the system gets stuck blowing only hot air or only cold air regardless of temperature settings. A characteristic clicking or tapping sound from behind the dashboard is the telltale sign of a failing actuator. The plastic gears inside the actuator are undersized and strip easily, especially in extreme temperatures.
records.solution: Replace the blend door actuator ($20-$50 for the part). On the Fiesta, the actuator is located behind the center of the dashboard and requires partial dash disassembly to access ($150-$400 labor at a shop). DIY-capable owners can do this in 1-2 hours following online guides. The Dorman replacement actuator is a popular upgrade as it uses more durable gears than the OEM part.
symptoms: Clicking or tapping noise from behind the dashboard when adjusting temperature
HVAC blows only hot air regardless of temperature setting
HVAC blows only cold air even when heat is selected
Temperature changes randomly without touching controls
Defrost does not work properly due to incorrect air routing

communityRecommendations.content: The clicking sound means the actuator gears are stripped — it will only get worse. A Dorman 604-252 or equivalent aftermarket actuator is $25 on Amazon and is more durable than OEM. Watch YouTube guides specific to the Fiesta for dash removal steps before attempting the repair.

records.title: Coil Spring Fracture — Snapped Suspension Spring
records.description: The suspension coil springs fracture, typically near the bottom coil, often triggered by corrosion at the spring seat combined with road-input stress from speed bumps and rough surfaces. This is a very frequently reported Fiesta failure — front springs are most commonly cited but rears also fail. A snapped spring can cut into the tire and causes uneven ride height, a lean to one side, clunking/creaking, and unstable handling. Corroded spring isolators (rubber seats) commonly fail alongside the spring. Ford issued a technical bulletin (TSB 3/2008) advising a zinc plate at the spring seat.
records.solution: Replace the fractured coil spring — replacing in axle pairs is recommended for even ride height — and fit new spring isolators/seats. Inspect the tire for spring-contact damage. On corrosion-belt cars, treat/clean the spring seats and use the zinc-plate/isolator upgrade.
symptoms: Car sits lower or leans to one side
Creaking or squeaking from a corner
Tire sidewall/tread damage from a broken coil

records.title: Door Latch Failure — Doors May Open While Driving
records.description: Ford recalled over 2 million vehicles including 2011-2015 Fiesta sedans and hatchbacks because of faulty door latches that can break internally. When the latch fails, the door may not close securely or may open unexpectedly while the vehicle is moving. The problem is caused by a pawl spring tab that can fracture inside the latch mechanism, particularly in warm climate states where heat accelerates material degradation. Ford issued multiple recalls (20S15, 20S30) to address this safety hazard.
records.solution: Contact your Ford dealer to check if your Fiesta is covered under recall 20S15 or 20S30 (NHTSA 20V177000, 20V331). Ford will replace the affected door latches free of charge. Do not ignore a door that does not close properly or makes unusual sounds when closing. If your Fiesta was previously registered in warm-climate states (AZ, CA, FL, TX, etc.), it is especially likely to be affected even if it is now in a cooler climate.
symptoms: Door does not latch securely on first attempt
Door ajar warning light stays on even when door appears closed
Door pops open while driving over bumps or during turns
Difficulty closing the door — requires extra force or multiple slams
Clicking or unusual sound from door latch mechanism

records.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Assist Fault — Sudden Loss of Assist
records.description: Fiestas can display 'Power Steering Assist Fault — Service Required' and lose electric power-steering assist, sometimes intermittently while driving. Root causes include torque-sensor faults and intermittent electrical connections in the steering column/gear that stop the control module from commanding the assist motor. When assist drops out the wheel becomes very heavy (manual mode), and some owners report the wheel jerking or pulling; Ford's broader EPS defects have driven multiple recalls and legal actions across its lineup. This is a safety-relevant electrical/steering failure.
records.solution: Scan the EPS module for fault codes and check steering-column/gear connectors and the torque sensor for intermittent connections. Reseat/repair wiring and clear codes; if the fault persists, the steering gear or EPS motor/torque-sensor assembly typically needs replacement (or software update where a campaign applies). Verify any open Ford steering campaign by VIN.
symptoms: Steering suddenly heavy / loss of assist
Assist restored after restart then recurs

records.title: Electronic Throttle Body Failure — Sudden Limp Mode & Wrench Light
records.description: The drive-by-wire electronic throttle body (ETB) develops an internal electronic/motor fault (not just dirt) that causes the powertrain control module to command reduced power. The car drops into limp mode with a wrench/powertrain-malfunction light, often storing throttle-position or actuator-control codes. Because the failure is internal to the unit, cleaning does not fix it. This is a recognized Ford-family ETB problem shared with Focus, Escape, Fusion and Transit Connect, and is reported by Fiesta owners including on the 1.6L engines.
records.solution: Replace the electronic throttle body with an updated OEM/Motorcraft unit and perform the throttle-relearn/idle-relearn procedure afterward to prevent high idle and drivability faults. Cleaning is not a durable fix once the internal fault is present.
symptoms: Sudden loss of power / limp mode while driving

records.title: Fiesta ST Rear Motor Mount (Dogbone) Bushing Failure — Vibration & Wheel Hop
records.description: The Fiesta ST's soft OEM rear motor mount (RMM / 'dogbone') bushing cannot withstand the 1.6L EcoBoost's torque and the high heat at its location, so the rubber degrades and allows excessive engine movement. This produces clunking on throttle on/off, driveline shudder, and wheel hop under hard acceleration, and accelerates wear on the remaining mounts. It is one of the most-discussed Fiesta ST maintenance items; owners commonly fit a polyurethane insert or an upgraded mount to eliminate the slop.
records.solution: Inspect the rear motor mount for torn/collapsed rubber and excessive engine rock. Install a polyurethane RMM insert or a stiffer upgraded rear motor mount to control engine movement; consider refreshing the full mount set if the others are also worn, since stiffening one loads the rest. Note added NVH is normal with stiffer bushings.
symptoms: Excessive engine rock when blipping throttle
Notchy engagement of gears at low speed

records.title: Ignition Coil / Spark Plug Misfire — Oil-Fouled Coils & Water Ingress in Plug Wells
records.description: Fiestas — especially the 1.6L EcoBoost ST — commonly throw misfire codes and run rough at idle from failing ignition coils and fouled spark plugs. Owners report oil creeping onto the coil boots and, notably, rainwater entering the spark-plug wells via the washer-jet routing, which soaks the plugs/coils and causes cylinder-specific misfires. Direct-injection combustion also makes the EcoBoost more prone to a slightly lumpy cold idle. Left unaddressed, a persistent misfire can trigger limp mode.
records.solution: Read misfire codes to identify the cylinder. Inspect plug wells for water/oil intrusion; if water is present, seal the washer-jet path and dry the wells. Replace fouled spark plugs with the correct heat range and gap, and replace failed coils (clean oil-contaminated boots or replace). Fix any upstream oil leak so coils don't re-foul. Clear codes and road-test.
symptoms: Water or oil found in spark-plug wells

records.title: Manual Transmission Clutch Judder & Slave/Release Cylinder Failure
records.description: Manual-transmission Fiestas (5-speed B5/IB5) commonly develop clutch judder, a soft/sinking pedal, and inability to select gears when the concentric slave/release cylinder or clutch master cylinder fails. Owners report the clutch going to the floor when stopped and gears becoming impossible to select, sometimes temporarily restored by restarting. Because the slave cylinder is inside the bellhousing, replacement requires removing the transaxle, so labor is significant. Contributing factors include worn or dislodged master-cylinder internals, contaminated hydraulic fluid, and normal clutch wear producing judder on take-up.
records.solution: Diagnose the hydraulic clutch: bleed and check for a firm pedal; if fluid loss or a sinking pedal is present, replace the concentric slave/release cylinder (transaxle out) and, when the box is out, replace the clutch disc, pressure plate, and release bearing as a set. Inspect/replace the clutch master cylinder and flush with correct-spec fluid. Address judder by replacing a glazed/contaminated clutch and checking engine/gearbox mounts.
symptoms: Clutch pedal sinks to floor / stays down
Judder or shudder when releasing the clutch
Difficulty or inability to select gears
Clutch bites very high or slips

records.title: Power Window Regulator / Cable Failure — Glass Drops Into Door
records.description: The plastic-geared window motor cog and the regulator's lift cables/clips wear or break, causing the window to fall inside the door, stick partway, or move only after repeated button presses. A characteristic symptom is a clicking/chattering or grinding noise as the glass jams or slips off its carrier. Commonly affects the driver's door (highest cycle count) but occurs on all doors, and the 3-door glass is frequently cited. Distinct from a purely electrical (switch/fuse) fault — the motor often runs while the glass does not move because the cable/cog has failed.
records.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly (regulator + motor as a unit is common); re-seat the glass on the carrier and verify the cables/clips. Where only the motor cog is stripped, a new motor/regulator cures it. Check the switch and one-touch initialization after repair.

records.title: DPS6 PowerShift Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder, Slipping, and Failure
records.description: The Ford Fiesta equipped with the DPS6 PowerShift dual-clutch automatic transmission is one of the most complained-about vehicles in recent history. The dry dual-clutch design causes severe shuddering, jerking, hesitation, and complete loss of power during acceleration. The clutch plates overheat and wear prematurely, often before 50,000 miles. The Transmission Control Module (TCM) software frequently fails to adapt properly, causing delayed shifts, harsh engagement, and rollback on hills. Ford faced a class-action lawsuit involving nearly 1.5 million vehicles and a federal settlement was reached.
records.solution: Check if your vehicle is covered under Ford's extended warranty or class-action settlement — many Fiestas qualify for free clutch and TCM replacement. If out of warranty, have the clutch assembly and TCM reprogrammed or replaced ($1,500-$3,500). Some owners have had success with multiple TCM reflashes to improve shift quality. As a last resort, some owners have converted to a manual transmission. Avoid the PowerShift entirely when purchasing a used Fiesta — manual transmission models are far more reliable.
symptoms: Violent shuddering or bucking during acceleration from a stop
Transmission slipping and RPMs flaring without acceleration
Harsh or jerky shifts between 1st and 2nd gear
Hesitation or delayed engagement when pressing the gas pedal
Vehicle rolls backward on hills even with foot on gas
Grinding or chattering noise from transmission area
Wrench warning light or transmission malfunction message

citations.title: Ford Fiesta PowerShift Transmission NHTSA Complaints

records.title: Rear Suspension Knock — Worn Rear Shock Top Mounts & Damper Bushings
records.description: Fiestas (2008–2019, including ST) frequently develop knocking, clunking, or scrubbing noises from the rear suspension over bumps. Common causes are worn rear shock-absorber top mounts, deteriorated damper eye/lower-mount bushings, and torn rubber that lets the shock move in its mount. Owners also find rattling heat shields and, occasionally, a broken coil-spring fragment knocking in the lower mount. It is a wear-and-tear NVH issue rather than a catastrophic failure, but it is one of the most-searched Fiesta annoyances.
records.solution: Inspect the rear shocks for oil leaks, torn/perished top-mount and eye bushings, and play in the mount. Replace worn rear shock absorbers (typically in pairs) along with their top mounts and bushings. Check for a cracked coil spring and loose/rattling rear heat shields, and re-secure or replace as needed.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking over bumps from the rear

records.title: SYNC / APIM Infotainment Freezing, Rebooting & Bluetooth/CarPlay Dropouts
records.description: Fiesta SYNC/MyFord Touch and SYNC 3 systems commonly freeze, randomly reboot, drop Bluetooth pairing, and lose Apple CarPlay connectivity. Many failures are software 'handshake' hangs, but a subset are hardware failures of the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM), which can enter a 'zombie' state where it draws power but the UI is frozen and soft resets do nothing. Symptoms include black screens, disappearing menus, unresponsive buttons, and USB ports that stop charging. A physical APIM fuse-pull/hard reboot resolves most connectivity hangs; persistent freezing points to APIM hardware or corrupted firmware.
records.solution: First perform a SYNC soft reset (hold Power + Seek-Right until reboot) and a master reset to clear corrupt Bluetooth profiles. Update SYNC firmware via USB with Ford's official update. For a frozen/zombie module, do a hardware reboot by pulling the APIM fuse. If freezing, black screens, or dead USB ports persist, replace/reflash the APIM module at a dealer.

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure — Stall Without Warning (Recall 15V005000)
records.description: Improper nickel plating of internal components in the Bosch in-tank fuel pump can cause the pump to fail, letting the engine stall without warning and increasing crash risk. Ford issued NHTSA recall 15V005000 covering certain 2014-2015 Fiesta (and related Fusion/MKZ) vehicles built spring 2014; the recall was first announced January 2015 and later expanded April 30, 2015. Owners report intermittent no-start and stalling. Outside the recall window, general in-tank pump wear produces similar hot-restart/low-pressure symptoms.
records.solution: For affected VINs, Ford dealers replace the fuel pump free of charge under recall 15V005000 — verify the VIN via NHTSA/Ford lookup. For out-of-recall failures, replace the in-tank pump module and check the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) where fitted. Confirm fuel-rail pressure after repair.
symptoms: Engine stalls without warning while driving
Loss of power / sputtering under load

records.title: TDCi Diesel DPF Blockage & Failed Regeneration (Short-Trip Use)
records.description: Diesel Fiestas frequently suffer diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage and incomplete/failed regeneration, especially on cars used mainly for short, low-speed journeys that never reach regeneration temperature. Soot accumulates, the DPF warning light appears, and the car may enter limp mode or dump excess fuel into the oil during failed active regens (raising oil level and diluting it). Underlying triggers are often other faults — a leaking/faulty injector, stuck EGR, blocked intake, or failed DPF differential-pressure/EGT sensor — so the blocked DPF is frequently a symptom rather than the root cause.
records.solution: When the DPF light shows, drive at a steady 40+ mph for ~20 minutes to allow passive/active regeneration before it fully blocks. If blocked, run a forced regeneration and diagnose the root cause: test the DPF pressure and EGT sensors, check EGR operation, and inspect for a leaking injector causing oil dilution. Clean or replace the DPF if soot loading is beyond limits, and change oil if fuel-diluted.
symptoms: Poor fuel economy after failed regen

records.title: Water Leak Into Footwell — Blocked Scuttle Drain / Pollen-Filter Housing
records.description: Fiestas commonly get wet passenger (and sometimes driver) footwell carpets from rainwater entering via the scuttle panel at the base of the windscreen. Leaves and debris block the scuttle drain, or the scuttle-to-windscreen seal fails, letting water pool and overflow into the cabin heater/pollen-filter housing and down into the footwell. The soaked carpet can cause musty smells, foggy windows, and electrical corrosion in floor connectors. It affects multiple generations and is a top owner complaint.
records.solution: Clear leaves/soil from the scuttle drain flaps and drainage channels, and reseal the scuttle panel to the windscreen where the seal has failed. Confirm the pollen/cabin-filter housing is sealed and draining. Dry the carpet fully (lift carpet, extract water, dehumidify) and check floor electrical connectors for corrosion.

records.title: Wet Belt (Belt-in-Oil) Timing Belt Degradation Clogging Oil Pump Pickup
records.description: The 1.0L EcoBoost uses a 'wet' timing belt that runs submerged in engine oil. When oil is old, over-extended, or not to Ford's WSS-M2C948-B spec, the belt's rubber breaks down and delaminates ('pilling'). Shed fragments migrate through the sump and clog the oil pump pickup screen, causing loss of oil pressure and catastrophic engine failure. NHTSA opened an investigation after dozens of complaints of low oil pressure followed by power loss on 1.0L EcoBoost vehicles. Ford originally quoted a very long belt interval (10 yr / 150k mi) but real-world failures pushed independent shops to recommend ~6 yr / 60k mi replacement. Failure can also destroy the belt-driven oil pump and cause the crank pulley to shed the belt.
records.solution: Replace the wet timing belt on a shortened interval (roughly every 6 years / 60,000 miles), and always use only the Ford-specified low-additive oil. At belt replacement, drop the sump and clean/replace the oil pump pickup screen and inspect for rubber debris. If low oil pressure or belt debris is found, replace the oil pump and pickup and flush the system; severe cases with bearing damage need engine replacement.
